title: Identifying Transported Mediation Effects after Aggregate Release and Deletion of Mediator Records
banked_reason: D0.5.G normalized tier incremental below field floor: paper score ceiling 4.8 < 7.4; finite certificate assumes release-known operator types and overlap tables, and finite-feature release includes target matrix; three panel findings and two witness setup defects remain.
gap_reasons: The headline variable-image theorem reduces to the general set-theoretic fact that law-specific maps glue exactly when they agree on every pairwise overlap
The advertised finite certificate assumes that the complete operator-type list, factor-map evaluations, and overlap-spanning vectors are already release-known
The finite-feature theorem further places every entry of both L_J(P) and the target matrix T(P) in the mediator-only release
The headline formula G_xi(s)+zeta is defined by choosing a compatible deleted law P and its h_P; outside the added finite-type hypothesis the core gives no release-only evaluation procedure
The Legendre construction never specializes the global outcome space H to contain P_2
The bump construction yields g_sep in C-infinity, but the core permits an arbitrary H subset of C(M); it need not contain g_sep
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the exact joint-fiber gluing equivalence, a connected-overlap transfer corollary, and finite-feature row-space reconstruction, then received an incremental tier at D0.5 against the field floor. The finite certificate leaves its operator types release-known by assumption, and the finite-feature release contains the target matrix; no bounded repair reached the field tier. Two companion witness theorems also need narrower outcome-space assumptions before their stated proofs are sound; this is an archived research draft, not a verified paper.
tldr: Deleting mediator records after a finite aggregate release leaves an entire mediator-law fiber, so fixed-law row-space factorization is not enough. The headline result is an exact gluing characterization: the law-specific target maps must agree on every overlap of feasible release ranges, even when their operator images vary. Under a common image, if the graph of spanning overlaps is connected, uniform point identification is equivalent to the existence of one common linear transfer; this connectivity condition strictly weakens the earlier constant-regression anchor, which is retained only as an easy design corollary. For \(N\) finite operator types, at most \(KJ\binom{N}{2}\) scalar overlap equalities suffice. Finite-feature reconstruction, cell-local release cost, and smooth positive nonidentification twins remain companion results. No privacy, deployment, estimator, finite-sample, efficiency, or general optimization claim is made.
gap: Full-data mediation formulas identify transported natural means when mediator laws remain available. Moment balancing, coarsening correction, separate-source mediation, Space Cover, and the matrix mechanism each address adjacent problems, but none supplies an exact compatibility criterion across every mediator law left possible by a declared aggregate deletion interface.
fill: The contribution separates fixed-law factorization from cross-law identification, derives a necessary and sufficient common-transfer formula in a broad positive-density regime, and characterizes the exact attainable cell-local cost of finite-feature repairs. The finite-probe certificate supplies a sufficient repair under an explicit structural span. The Legendre and unrestricted finite-probe theorems remain subordinate internal boundary results that delimit failure of this paper's declared release interface and make no claim against published estimators, workflows, or post-deletion guarantees.
